gen-gf-aboreto-roboto-slab: Aboreto spreads wide, ladle-shaped bowls across generous gaps, all display swagger, while Roboto Slab keeps its slab-serif body precise and structured. Shrink that heading and the swagger fades.
gen-gf-aboreto-rubik: Hairline serifs perch on very thick stems in Aboreto, which gives the heading its odd, commanding look. And Rubik, a soft sans with round, open letters, keeps the text clear underneath.
gen-gf-adamina-fs-bespoke-sans: Bespoke Sans arrives sharp and refined, with generous room where its curves meet the stem, under an Adamina heading that has a bookish, editorial feel. Their styles differ, and that difference is the draw.
gen-gf-advent-pro-fs-literata: Literata reads sophisticated and bookish, its strokes thickening and thinning gently. Advent Pro above it keeps one unchanging line weight with brush-lifted curve ends, and made small it would lose its presence beside that body.
gen-gf-afacad-fs-literata: Afacad draws its sans-serif letters with a single plotter-pen line, no hairlines to squint at, over a body in Literata. A classic serif like that settles into a warm, bookish reading rhythm.
gen-gf-afacad-flux-fs-literata: Afacad Flux cuts every curve at one flat line width, like sign-shop vinyl, with open bowls that welcome the eye. Literata's text serif, with moderate stroke contrast and wide curved mouths, makes extended reading feel sophisticated and bookish.
gen-gf-agdasima-fs-literata: Contemporary and clean, Agdasima packs tight gaps and zero stroke contrast into its heading. Literata's serif body does the opposite job, letting a modest weight shift inside each stroke carry the reading.
gen-gf-akatab-fs-literata: Open-aperture curves run through every letter of Akatab, giving the heading a modern, contemporary feel. And Literata, a classic serif with middling contrast like a half-turned flat brush, gives the page a bookish counterweight.
gen-gf-akshar-fs-literata: Literata reads sophisticated and bookish, with moderate contrast that is neither stark nor flat. Akshar, with letters crowding each other's edges, makes a modern, tight heading against that classic serif softness.
gen-gf-alata-fs-literata: Plainness is Alata's whole trick, a modern, approachable heading with almost no modulation. Literata brings light modulation as a text serif, and that gentle shift is what the pair does best.
